clue.text: High-rise flat in the country

parts.note: reads like a tower-block apartment out in the shires, but describes an area of land that is raised and level

explanation.surface: A tower-block apartment somewhere out in rural parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a home in a tall block; here it is level ground, and 'high-rise' means raised up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableland is an expanse of elevated, level terrain.

clue.text: For French scientist, fake gem takes half an hour

parts.note: paste is glass used to imitate gemstones

indicators.note: only the second half of the word hour is taken, its last two letters

explanation.surface: A French scientist's imitation jewel consumes thirty minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' simply joins the pieces; 'half' picks the back half of 'hour'.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist behind pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: Shaver depilates roughly strapping needed!

indicators.note: roughly signals that the letters of the two words are only approximately in order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who removes hair crudely ends up needing a bandage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges all fifteen letters of SHAVER and DEPILATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticking plaster on a fabric backing is used as strapping to bind wounds or joints.

clue.text: English these days is enough for poets

parts.note: at present, currently

explanation.surface: Modern English suffices for verse writers.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic, poetic form meaning sufficient.

clue.text: You flog about looking for things in the sky

definitions.text: looking for things in the sky

indicators.note: about here means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: You whip around while searching for objects overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the seven letters of YOU FLOG.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of reported flying saucers and alien craft is a search for objects in the heavens.

clue.text: One of a set of small pliers on the radio?

definitions.text: One of a set of small pliers on the radio?

parts.words: One of a set of small pliers on the radio?
parts.note: reads like a toolkit item heard about on air, but a plier is one who plies for hire, and these small hire cars are booked by radio

explanation.surface: A little gripping tool being talked about on the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pliers' is not the tool but people who ply a trade; a small car plying for hire and dispatched by two-way radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A small private-hire taxi, booked by phone and dispatched by radio.

clue.text: Hot Stuff top per. 2 former in very soft ground

indicators.note: in places the performer within the soft ground

parts.note: mud is very soft, wet earth
a star is a leading performer

explanation.surface: A sizzling celebrity sinks into a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'per. 2 former' is a print garble of 'performer'.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow condiment is a famously pungent, fiery relish.

clue.text: Innocent abroad?

parts.note: an unworldly person, described in a foreign language, since the word is French

explanation.surface: A naive tourist overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' hints that the word for an innocent is a borrowing from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive or artless, the French adjective used in English for an unsophisticated person.

clue.text: Victoria's sonnet about "Friend of the Earth"

indicators.note: about means the letters of the queen's poem are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A queen writes a poem concerning an environmental campaign group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges VICTORIAS SONNET; Friends of the Earth is an environmental campaign group, so one of its members is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An environmentalist works to protect nature, as a friend of the planet would.

clue.text: He can came a horse — a white horse?

definitions.meaning: one who breaks in horses for riding

explanation.surface: A trainer gentles a pale mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white horses' are crested waves rolling in.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-breaker trains a wild horse, and a large wave crashing on shore is also so called.

clue.text: Organised forms of technology?

parts.note: forms are classes in a school, so organised classes in technical subjects make an institution

explanation.surface: Structured types of engineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forms' are school classes, not types or shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic institution devoted to teaching sciences, with classes in technical subjects.

clue.text: Poetry unopened it's in Gaelic

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A poem left unread is in an old Celtic tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional name for the Goidelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Kind of anaesthetic for the pub

definitions.meaning: one that numbs only part of the body
one's nearest drinking house, in British usage

explanation.surface: Something to numb you, or the nearby bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain one's regular nearby pub is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbing agent applied to one area, and a neighbourhood tavern.

clue.text: Put on common ground

definitions.meaning: slang for the floor, as in hitting it

explanation.surface: Laid upon shared territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to adorn or clothe, and the floor is the deck when you hit it.

clue.text: South Sea hail and farewell

parts.note: a Pacific island greeting that serves for both hello and goodbye

explanation.surface: A Polynesian welcome and send-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hail' is a greeting, not icy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian word is used both to greet and to bid goodbye.

clue.text: Lager-brewing produces this 0 fierce stare

indicators.note: brewing suggests the beer's letters are being stirred and mixed into another form

explanation.surface: Making beer causes an angry look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' rearranges LAGER; the stray 0 is a print speck.
explanation.definitionFit: An angry, piercing look is a glower.

clue.text: Means of turning back on railway it is great fun

indicators.note: back means the word for the turning tool is read in reverse

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to turn or prise

explanation.surface: A track switch on the line is a real thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LEVER into REVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Merrymaking and festivity are lively enjoyment.

clue.text: Bowl with hand over?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to send the ball to the batsman
to pass something on to its recipient

explanation.surface: A cricket ball sent down by a bowler with a raised arm.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler's ball is called a delivery, and bowlers bowl overarm, hence 'hand over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler sends down the ball, and a courier conveys goods to someone.

clue.text: Ginger-beer stall run by uncle

definitions.meaning: pop is fizzy soft drink, so a place selling it
uncle is slang for a pawnbroker, and pop means to pawn

explanation.surface: A relative runs the soft-drink kiosk.
explanation.walkthrough: In old British slang 'uncle' is the pawnbroker and to 'pop' something is to pawn it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk selling fizzy drinks, and a pawnbroker's premises in slang.

clue.text: One to 16 mail — he gets stick

parts.note: a post is a stake or stick
a man is a he

explanation.surface: The carrier of letters is bitten, or beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is DELIVER, so the definition reads 'one to deliver mail'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail carrier brings letters to houses.

clue.text: First school colour

definitions.meaning: the first school a child attends
red, yellow or blue, from which others are mixed

explanation.surface: The opening day's paint lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal; the elementary school; and a base hue such as red or blue.

clue.text: Whirls at extremely giddy speeds

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme, first and last, letters of giddy

parts.note: rates are speeds

explanation.surface: Spinning at dizzying velocity.
explanation.definitionFit: Spins round and round, revolving.

clue.text: Light worker found in the bay perhaps

definitions.text: Light worker found in the bay perhaps

parts.words: Light worker found in the bay perhaps
parts.note: lights are window panes, and a bay is a kind of window, so the tradesman fitting panes

explanation.surface: A lightweight labourer down at the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' means a window pane, not lightweight, and 'bay' is a window, not the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fits panes of glass into windows.

clue.text: Advanced class remains disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of the word are knocked out of place

explanation.surface: A higher-level group's leftovers are upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges REMAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial group of advanced students discussing a topic.

clue.text: Blow not unwelcome on the back

definitions.text: Blow not unwelcome on the back

parts.words: Blow not unwelcome on the back
parts.note: a pat given between the shoulders as congratulation, a friendly hit

explanation.surface: A friendly pat between the shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: One kind of this blow, on the back, is a gesture of congratulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack with the open hand, welcome when it congratulates.

clue.text: Gold sovereign

parts.note: a sovereign is a king, and this legendary king turned everything to gold

explanation.surface: An old British gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is a British gold coin, but here it means a king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phrygian king of myth whose touch turned things to bullion.

clue.text: Chamber for Othello retiring?

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Shakespeare's Othello is the Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: A bedroom for Shakespeare's general to go to bed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is an enclosed space in a building.

clue.text: It could be taken from the garden-centre early

definitions.text: It could be taken from the garden-centre early

indicators.note: taken from shows the letters are lifted out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A plant bought from a nursery ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' pulls the letters out across 'centRE Early'; the whole clue is also a description of a sapling bought at a nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapling is a typical purchase carried home from a plant nursery.

clue.text: Ireland's county of springtime love

parts.note: May is a spring month
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: An Irish region that lives for spring romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is one of the counties on Ireland's west coast.

clue.text: Becoming somebody? Aim is alien to art perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters might form something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Turning into a person: an artistic aim that is foreign to art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges AIM IS ALIEN TO ART; a ghost becoming 'some body' takes physical form.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking bodily form is what a spirit does when it appears in the flesh.

clue.text: Place or race for two year-olds

definitions.meaning: a place for very young children, or for raising plants
a horse race restricted to two-year-old horses

explanation.surface: A venue or contest for toddlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two year-olds' suggests toddlers, but in racing two-year-old horses run in nursery handicaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A room or school for infants, and a handicap race for young horses.

clue.text: Nothing in duty list for the home bird

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the list of duties

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nobody on the rota for the stay-at-home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home bird' suggests a stay-at-home person, but it is the farmyard cock that comes home to roost.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is a domestic fowl kept at the farm.
